content:
olivia: thinking out loud — can we drop the protobuf gateway shim and move to a shimless routing model for internal APIs? pros: fewer translation layers, less perf tax. cons: client ergonomics and browser support for streaming gRPC.

mike: +1 on slimming the stack but worried about API ergonomics. a lot of our frontend clients expect JSON over HTTP. we need a clear fallback path (transcode? gateway?).

jana: main concerns: quota propagation and telemetry. if we remove the shim, how do we consistently carry tenant headers and sampling hints through the stack? current shim normalizes those.

olivia: right — headers like x-tenant-id, x-request-origin, and our sampling hints are critical for console dashboards and per-route costing. if shimless, runtime needs to enforce envelope conventions.

sam: can we standardize an HTTP/JSON envelope that both native gRPC clients and browser clients use? e.g.:

```json
{
  "envelope": {"tenant":"t-123", "trace_hint":"sampler=1/100"},
  "payload": { /* proto-json */ }
}
```

sam: gateway only needs to unwrap/validate the envelope when present. that keeps the path simple and still supports legacy clients.

mike: that works but now every service has to validate the envelope. do we want to push that to a shared middleware lib? we already have dozens of microservices.

jana: yes, middleware lib + strong test harness. also add an E2E check in the console rollout that ensures traces and quota tags show up in telemetry before we flip traffic.

olivia: +1. UX for rollouts: we should have a console toggle to enable shimless mode per route with a rollout % and rollback button. console should show a realtime heatmap of failed envelope validations and quota errors.

sam: about quotas — enforcement at edge vs service: if edge enforces, cheaper to reject early, but metrics for consumed tokens need to be sent downstream so billing/console matches reality. tricky.

jana: telemetry pipeline needs a small message contract: when edge accepts/rejects, emit an event with fields: route_id, tenant, action (accept/reject), reason, timestamp. console can then reconcile.

mike: also watch out for streaming RPCs — browsers + SSE/WS vs HTTP2 gRPC. If we keep shimless, streaming clients must use gRPC-web or a small streaming adapter. that's a hard ops story.

olivia: proposal: 1) POC on two internal routes (embed + async-rerank) with shimless envelope. 2) shared middleware lib for envelope validation + header wiring. 3) console rollout toggle + signal dashboards (envelope failures, quota rejects, sampling coverage). 4) keep a tiny adapter for browser streaming (gRPC-web) until client libs roll forward.

sam: can we add a canary signal to the routing policy config? something like:

```yaml
route: /v2/embed
routing_policy:
  mode: shimless
  rollout: 10% # weighted routing
  fallback: proto-gateway
  signals:
    - envelope_failures
    - quota_reject_rate
    - trace_coverage
```

jana: perfect — console can auto-create alerts on those signals if thresholds exceed X. also capture a sample of the failing payloads (PII scrubbed) for easier debugging.

mike: final note: backward compat. we should version the envelope and prefer RPC contract changes over silent breaking. add an "envelope_version" header so older services still accept.

olivia: agreed. next steps: @sam can you spin up POC, @jana add telemetry schema, @mike coordinate client compatibility plan. i'll file an RFC with the rollout UX mockups.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/proxy-adapter/poC -> staging (job #4821).

sam: started POC branch: https://git/redwood/infra/proxy-adapter/pulls/42 — added middleware + example route.

jana: will draft telemetry schema and a console signal dashboard tomorrow morning.

mike: i'll audit top-10 frontend consumers to see who needs gRPC-web or adapter changes.

olivia: thanks all — aim to have green e2e telemetry before expanding rollout. :thumbsup:
